geometry: Prescribed Schein-Aichelburg same-exterior MP/shell/RN handle; SA v5 two-input RN scattering is frozen as a completed subcomponent.
matter_content: Classical charged shells and Maxwell background; neutral real massless minimally coupled scalar signal; two external source ports; finite Ramsey qubit receiver; ordinary classical memory.
quantum_state: One operation-independent centered Gaussian seed on the modeled field algebra, with bit-antisymmetric coherent displacement. The C proof is independent of the unknown numerical seed variance.
topology: Same exterior is connected through the prescribed SA handle; ordinary MP exterior path carries the stored receiver record forward to the sender.
assumptions: SA v5 inverse scattering is accepted as a completed subcomponent; no further pulse-shape optimization is used.
The future sender can causally control both external source ports before their emissions.
The global probability/process law is linear, normalized and independent of which local future CPTP operation is selected.
Past receiver records can be stored and transported ordinarily forward to the future laboratory.
Standard local copy and NOT measure-and-prepare operations are admissible.
boundary_conditions: Use the fixed SA v5 shell/RN mode interfaces and the same Gaussian seed for both bits; no future-operation-dependent boundary condition or postselection.
symmetries: No new symmetry beyond the frozen SA v5 component; the operational closure is binary but does not replace the 3+1D spacetime by a 1+1D theory.
approximation_order: Exact binary process-normalization algebra on top of the frozen linear 4D signal component; not a full nonlinear semiclassical evolution.

stress_energy.formula: The two bit states differ by opposite coherent means over one seed; the C proof uses only the induced finite-receiver kernel and does not assign an unknown RSET the value zero.

backreaction.details: Formation/backreaction remain unresolved in SA generally, but even granting the fixed background and two-port propagation cannot yield D_past>0 under the stated operation-composition assumptions.

support_accounting.details: SA formation and apparatus budgets are not completed; they are granted rather than used as the obstruction.

stability: Not the active obstruction. The result is a normalization/composability obstruction for the closed intervention model.
causal_structure: Past receiver R precedes future sender S along an ordinary exterior path; the SA handle supplies the candidate return influence S -> R. Closing R -> S memory and S -> R candidate channel creates the tested loop.

sender_intervention.description: At future station S, do(b) writes b∈{0,1} to one classical controller. Ordinary forward control lines drive two source ports: F_A^(b)=(-1)^b conjugate(T) g and F_B^(b)=-(-1)^b R g. Each port applies the corresponding Weyl displacement. No postselection.

receiver_observable: Finite worldtube Ramsey qubit initially |+x>, U_R=exp[-i lambda sigma_z Phi(F)], sigma_y measurement with all Y=±1 outcomes stored.

P_Y_do_0.derivation: Closed-process normalization with admissible copy and NOT future controllers forces d=0.

P_Y_do_1.derivation: Closed-process normalization with admissible copy and NOT future controllers forces d=0.

distinguishability.derivation: Open Ramsey kernel has D=|d|; closed copy/NOT history totals are 1+d and 1-d, so normalization of both forces d=0.

obstructions: For the open receiver kernel K(r|b)=[1+(-1)^(r+b)d]/2, closing the stored record through copy gives Z=1+d and through NOT gives Z=1-d.
One fixed operation-independent normalized process must normalize both admissible local operations; hence d=0.
Per-operation global renormalization changes the future controller distribution and is postselection/final-boundary behavior rather than the stated do-intervention.
unresolved_assumptions: SA formation, full RSET/backreaction and material stability remain unresolved but are not needed to derive this C.
Escapes require changing the model class: operation-dependent boundary/background, nonlinear/final-state rule, forbidden copy/NOT operations, or inability to preserve the receiver record.

quantitative_obstruction.attempted_nonzero_D_normalization_defect: exactly D for each of copy and NOT, with opposite signs
